items.claim: `Parser.parse_statement` dispatches keyword statements via `getattr(self, f"parse_{value}")`
items.label: supported
items.reason: parse_statement does `f = getattr(self, f"parse_{self.stream.current.value}")` for keywords in _statement_keywords.

items.claim: The Jinja lexer recognizes string literals in single and double quotes.
items.label: supported
items.reason: string_re matches both single-quoted and double-quoted literals and is registered as TOKEN_STRING in the tag rules.

items.claim: `PackageLoader` loads templates from a directory within a Python package using `importlib.resources`.
items.label: contradicted
items.reason: PackageLoader uses importlib.util.find_spec, import_module, zipimport and plain os file access, not importlib.resources.

items.claim: In `NativeEnvironment`, a dictionary renders as a Python dict rather than its string representation.
items.label: supported
items.reason: native_concat returns the raw single value unchanged when it is not a string, and the native code generator omits str() around output, so a dict stays a dict.

items.claim: The publishing workflow uses `uv build` and `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish`.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: The publish workflow file was not shown, so its build and publish steps cannot be checked.

items.claim: A second `{% extends %}` makes `visit_Extends` emit `raise TemplateRuntimeError("extended multiple times")` and raise `CompilerExit`
items.label: supported
items.reason: When extends_so_far > 0 the generator writes the 'extended multiple times' TemplateRuntimeError and raises CompilerExit when the extends is already known (rootlevel first extends).

items.claim: By default, blocks cannot access variables from outside their scope, such as loop variables.
items.label: supported
items.reason: Block functions get a fresh Frame deliberately not parented to the toplevel frame, and only `scoped` blocks get a derived context, so outer/loop variables are not available by default.

items.claim: `NativeEnvironment` is defined in nativetypes.py.
items.label: supported
items.reason: NativeEnvironment is declared in src/jinja2/nativetypes.py.

items.claim: `Context.globals_keys` is `set(globals)` and is used by `_get_default_module` to decide whether new globals require a fresh module instance
items.label: supported
items.reason: Context sets globals_keys = set(globals) and _get_default_module compares ctx.globals_keys to self.globals.keys() to build a fresh, uncached module.

items.claim: `Parser.subparse`'s main loop recognises only `data`, `variable_begin` and `block_begin` tokens, raising `AssertionError` for anything else
items.label: supported
items.reason: The subparse loop handles data, variable_begin and block_begin and raises AssertionError('internal parsing error') otherwise.

items.claim: If a filter is not found in `env.filters`, Jinja2 raises a `TemplateRuntimeError` or `UndefinedError`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: Missing filters raise TemplateRuntimeError both in _filter_test_common and in the generated runtime stub emitted by pull_dependencies.

items.claim: `Context.resolve_or_missing` checks `vars` first, then `parent`, and returns the `missing` sentinel if neither has the name
items.label: supported
items.reason: resolve_or_missing checks self.vars, then self.parent, and returns missing.

items.claim: `nodes.TemplateData.as_const` returns the template text wrapped in `Markup` when autoescaping is enabled
items.label: supported
items.reason: TemplateData.as_const returns Markup(self.data) when eval_ctx.autoescape is set.

items.claim: The `publish-pypi` job requires `id-token: write` permissions for the OIDC handshake.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: The publish workflow contents, including job permissions, were not shown.

items.claim: `uv.lock` is the deterministic lockfile for all development and test dependencies.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: No uv.lock appears in the repository listing and pyproject.toml was not shown, so the claim about a lockfile cannot be settled.

items.claim: The `is_undefined` utility in jinja2.utils checks if a value is an instance of `Undefined`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: is_undefined performs an isinstance check against runtime.Undefined.

items.claim: The `select` filter filters items based on a test.
items.label: supported
items.reason: sync_do_select applies a test via select_or_reject and yields only items passing it.

items.claim: `Environment.join_path` default implementation returns its first argument unchanged
items.label: supported
items.reason: join_path returns the `template` argument unchanged.

items.claim: `Parser.flush_data` wraps buffered nodes in an `Output` node and clears the buffer
items.label: supported
items.reason: The flush_data helper in Parser.subparse appends nodes.Output(data_buffer[:]) to the body and deletes the buffer contents (though it is a nested function, not a method).

items.claim: `Template.render` joins the generated stream with `self.environment.concat(...)`
items.label: supported
items.reason: render returns self.environment.concat(self.root_render_func(ctx)).

items.claim: `{{ user.url }}` is parsed via `parse_tuple` whose postfix parser produces `Getattr(node=Name('user','load'), attr='url')`
items.label: supported
items.reason: variable_begin calls parse_tuple, and parse_subscript on a dot+name token returns nodes.Getattr(node, attr, 'load').

items.claim: Variables assigned inside an `if` block persist in the outer scope.
items.label: supported
items.reason: visit_If compiles the body with a soft frame that shares the enclosing frame's symbols, so assignments inside an if persist outside it.

items.claim: If a required block has not been overridden when a template is rendered, Jinja raises a `TemplateRuntimeError`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: visit_Block emits code raising TemplateRuntimeError("Required block ... not found") when a required block has no override.

items.claim: `Parser.parse_statement` falls back to `self.extensions.get(token.value)` for custom tags
items.label: supported
items.reason: parse_statement looks up custom tags via self.extensions.get(token.value) and calls ext(self).

items.claim: The `auto_aiter` function in src/jinja2/async_utils.py supports iterating over both standard and asynchronous iterables.
items.label: supported
items.reason: auto_aiter returns the object's __aiter__ when present, otherwise wraps a sync iterator in _IteratorToAsyncIterator.

items.claim: When `is_async` is False the async-only runtime names are excluded from the generated import line
items.label: supported
items.reason: exported_names includes async_exported only when environment.is_async, otherwise only `exported` names are imported.

items.claim: `create_cache` returns `None` for a cache size of 0, disabling template caching
items.label: supported
items.reason: create_cache returns None when size == 0.

items.claim: The `xmlattr` filter converts a dict to XML attributes.
items.label: supported
items.reason: do_xmlattr builds a key="value" attribute string from a mapping's items.

items.claim: EditorConfig enforces 4 spaces for Python, 2 spaces for YAML/HTML, and LF line endings.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: The .editorconfig file contents were not shown.

items.claim: The extension hook `preprocess` modifies source text before lexing.
items.label: supported
items.reason: Extension.preprocess returns modified source and Environment._tokenize calls preprocess before lexer.tokenize.

items.claim: `CodeGenerator.__init__` attaches an `Optimizer` when `optimized` is True
items.label: supported
items.reason: CodeGenerator.__init__ sets self.optimizer = Optimizer(environment) when optimized is true.

items.claim: The `EvalContext` allows filters to check if autoescaping is currently active.
items.label: supported
items.reason: Filters decorated with @pass_eval_context inspect eval_ctx.autoescape to detect active autoescaping.

items.claim: `CodeGenerator.blockvisit` writes `pass` before walking the nodes
items.label: supported
items.reason: blockvisit writes 'pass' before visiting each node.

items.claim: The `@pass_context`, `@pass_eval_context`, and `@pass_environment` decorators are defined in `jinja2.utils`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: All three decorators are defined in src/jinja2/utils.py.

items.claim: The `xmlattr` filter disallows keys containing spaces or the characters `/`, `>`, or `=`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: _attr_key_re matches whitespace, '/', '>', and '=' in keys and do_xmlattr raises ValueError when it matches.

items.claim: `compiler.generate` returns `generator.stream.getvalue()`
items.label: supported
items.reason: generate returns generator.stream.getvalue() when no stream was given.

items.claim: With no extensions, `Environment.preprocess` collapses to `str(source)`
items.label: supported
items.reason: preprocess reduces over iter_extensions starting from str(source), so with no extensions it returns str(source).

items.claim: `CodeGenerator.visit_Template` emits the load name as `name = 'members.html'` for a template named members.html
items.label: supported
items.reason: visit_Template writes f"name = {self.name!r}", producing name = 'members.html'.

items.claim: The `for` loop iterates over sequences such as lists, dictionaries, or any iterable object.
items.label: supported
items.reason: LoopContext wraps any iterable via `iter(iterable)` and yields its items, so `for` works over lists, dicts, and other iterables.

items.claim: `trim_blocks` and `lstrip_blocks` can be enabled globally in the Environment.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The Environment constructor accepts `trim_blocks` and `lstrip_blocks` and stores them on the environment.

items.claim: `create_cache` returns a plain `dict` for a negative cache size, which never evicts
items.label: supported
items.reason: create_cache returns an empty dict for negative sizes, which performs no eviction.

items.claim: The generated block function header is `def block_title(context, missing=missing, environment=environment):`
items.label: supported
items.reason: Block functions are emitted as `def block_<name>(context, missing=missing, environment=environment):` since envenv is ', environment=environment' unless defer_init.

items.claim: Tests are mappings of test names to boolean callables.
items.label: supported
items.reason: TESTS is a dict mapping test names to callables returning booleans.

items.claim: `visit_Block` returns without writing anything when `frame.toplevel` and `has_known_extends` are both true
items.label: supported
items.reason: In visit_Block, when frame.toplevel and self.has_known_extends are true the method returns immediately before any write calls.

items.claim: `Parser.__init__` stores the name and filename and calls the environment to tokenize the source
items.label: supported
items.reason: Parser.__init__ sets self.name/self.filename and calls environment._tokenize(source, name, filename, state).

items.claim: `loop.index` is the current iteration, 1-indexed.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `index` is documented and implemented as `index0 + 1`, i.e. the current iteration starting at 1.

items.claim: `Template.is_up_to_date` calls the uptodate closure and compares the captured source against the mapping's current value
items.label: supported
items.reason: is_up_to_date invokes the stored _uptodate callable, and DictLoader's closure compares the captured source to self.mapping.get(template).

items.claim: The `Environment` constructor stores the `autoescape` argument without calling it
items.label: supported
items.reason: The constructor simply assigns self.autoescape = autoescape with no invocation.

items.claim: An empty data group is dropped by the lexer because `TOKEN_DATA` is in `ignore_if_empty`
items.label: supported
items.reason: ignore_if_empty contains TOKEN_DATA and the tokenizer only yields a group when `data or token not in ignore_if_empty`.

items.claim: The `@internalcode` decorator is defined in src/jinja2/utils.py.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `internalcode` is defined in utils.py.

items.claim: The symbol visitor in idtracking stops at `Block` nodes and does not descend into them
items.label: supported
items.reason: FrameSymbolVisitor.visit_Block is an empty method documented as 'Stop visiting at blocks.'

items.claim: The `length` filter returns the sequence length.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The FILTERS dict maps "length" to the builtin `len`.

items.claim: The `autoescape` parameter can be a boolean or a callable that takes a template name and returns a boolean.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The `autoescape` parameter is typed `bool | t.Callable[[str | None], bool]` and documented as accepting a callable given the template name.

items.claim: `EvalContext.__init__` calls `environment.autoescape` with the template name when it is callable
items.label: supported
items.reason: EvalContext.__init__ calls environment.autoescape(template_name) when the attribute is callable.

items.claim: The `Undefined` base class is defined in src/jinja2/runtime.py.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The `Undefined` class is defined in runtime.py.

items.claim: A `Frame` constructed with no parent creates a root `Symbols` at level 0
items.label: supported
items.reason: Frame with parent None builds Symbols(level=level); Symbols sets level 0 when both parent and level are None.

items.claim: `DictLoader.get_source` raises `TemplateNotFound(template)` when the name is not in the mapping
items.label: supported
items.reason: DictLoader.get_source raises TemplateNotFound(template) if the template is not a key of the mapping.

items.claim: `Environment.compile` catches only `TemplateSyntaxError` and re-raises it through `handle_exception`
items.label: supported
items.reason: compile wraps its body in `except TemplateSyntaxError: self.handle_exception(source=source_hint)` with no other handlers.

items.claim: `BytecodeCache` is defined in src/jinja2/bccache.py and is an interface for persisting compiled template bytecode.
items.label: supported
items.reason: bccache.py defines the BytecodeCache base class with load_bytecode/dump_bytecode for persisting compiled bytecode.

items.claim: `CodeGenerator.visit_Template` emits block functions after the root function, one per entry in `self.blocks` in `find_all` order
items.label: supported
items.reason: self.blocks is filled from node.find_all(nodes.Block) and block functions are emitted after the root function by iterating that dict in insertion order.

items.claim: `FileSystemLoader` has a `followlinks` parameter controlling whether to follow symbolic links.
items.label: supported
items.reason: FileSystemLoader takes `followlinks` and passes it to os.walk.

items.claim: The `Context` class tracks template inheritance through its `blocks` attribute.
items.label: supported
items.reason: Context.blocks holds a stack of block functions updated during template inheritance, used by `super`.

items.claim: `Environment.filters` defaults to `DEFAULT_FILTERS` defined in src/jinja2/defaults.py.
items.label: supported
items.reason: Environment sets `self.filters = DEFAULT_FILTERS.copy()` and DEFAULT_FILTERS is the name bound in defaults.py.

items.claim: `Environment.getattr` tries a real Python attribute first, falls back to item access, and returns an `Undefined` if both fail
items.label: supported
items.reason: getattr tries getattr(obj, attribute), then obj[attribute], then returns self.undefined(...).

items.claim: `Lexer.wrap` discards whitespace and comment tokens
items.label: supported
items.reason: wrap skips any token in ignored_tokens, which includes whitespace and the comment/linecomment tokens.

items.claim: `DictLoader.__init__` binds the mapping argument to `self.mapping` and returns without copying it
items.label: supported
items.reason: DictLoader.__init__ only does self.mapping = mapping, with no copy.

items.claim: A parent template's `visit_Block` generates `yield from context.blocks['title'][0](context)`
items.label: supported
items.reason: For a non-scoped, non-async, unbuffered block the generator writes `yield from context.blocks['title'][0](context)`.

items.claim: `Environment.make_globals(None)` returns `ChainMap({}, self.globals)`
items.label: supported
items.reason: make_globals replaces a None argument with {} and returns ChainMap(d, self.globals).

items.claim: The `super()` function renders the content of the parent block within an overriding block.
items.label: supported
items.reason: Context.super returns a BlockReference whose call renders the parent block's content.

items.claim: `CodeGenerator.visit_Template` writes the root function header `def root(context, missing=missing, environment=environment):` with `extra=1`
items.label: supported
items.reason: envenv is ', environment=environment' when not deferring init, and the root header is written with extra=1.

items.claim: The sandbox blocks the generator attributes `gi_frame` and `gi_code`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: UNSAFE_GENERATOR_ATTRIBUTES contains gi_frame and gi_code and is_internal_attribute flags them for generators.

items.claim: The tox configuration uses `uv-venv-lock-runner`.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: No tox configuration file is present in the shown repository contents, so the runner setting cannot be checked.

items.claim: If `auto_reload` is enabled in the Environment, the `uptodate` function is checked whenever a template is requested.
items.label: supported
items.reason: _load_template re-uses a cached template only if auto_reload is off or `template.is_up_to_date` (which calls the uptodate function) is true.

items.claim: Built-in filters are defined in filters.py and are usually prefixed with `do_` in the Python source code.
items.label: supported
items.reason: filters.py defines the built-in filters with `do_` prefixed function names registered in FILTERS.

items.claim: `Environment.from_string` creates a template from a string.
items.label: supported
items.reason: Environment.from_string compiles the source string and returns a Template instance.

items.claim: To create a custom loader, you subclass `BaseLoader` and override the `get_source` method.
items.label: supported
items.reason: BaseLoader's docstring and get_source explicitly instruct subclassing and overriding get_source.

items.claim: `visit_Extends` fails if `frame.toplevel` is not True
items.label: supported
items.reason: visit_Extends calls self.fail('cannot use extend from a non top-level scope') when frame.toplevel is falsy.

items.claim: `Environment._parse` constructs a `Parser` and calls its parse method
items.label: supported
items.reason: _parse returns Parser(self, source, name, filename).parse().

items.claim: `{% include ["page.html", "default.html"] %}` accepts a list of template names.
items.label: supported
items.reason: get_or_select_template dispatches lists of names to select_template, and Include nodes with tuple/list templates are handled accordingly.

items.claim: `visit_For` sets `extended_loop` False and emits an ordinary Python loop when the loop is not recursive, contains no scoped block, and the body does not use `loop`
items.label: supported
items.reason: extended_loop is only true for recursive loops, use of `loop` in the body, or scoped blocks; otherwise a plain `for ... in ...:` is emitted.
